newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Hang Seng at 15,000 Mar 98 - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Hang Seng at 15,000 Mar 98 - Salomon.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said it estimated the "fair value" of the Hang Seng Index at March 31, 1998, to be 15,000.
That would be a 23 percent total return over the 12 months to that date, comprising a three percent dividend yield and 20 percent price change, Salomon said in a recent report.
"In absolute and relative terms, Hong Kong's earnings prospects are some of the best in the region," Salomon said.
"Over the past few months, we have raised our market earnings growths forecasts to 19 percent from 11 percent in October 1996," it said.

Salomon said its model yielded a fair value estimate of 15.5 times price-earnings ratio (PER) in March 1998, and this combined with expected 19 percent earnings growth yielded the Hang Seng Index fair value close of 15,000 for March 31, 1998.
The main risk to its higher 15.5 times PER was accelerated global economic growth in 1998, but Salomon said its economists believed this was most unlikely.
It said it expected monetary tightening in the United States to be mild and finishing in calendar 1997.
Salomon said it was assuming unchanged political risk in Hong Kong over the next 12 months.
